scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0063; not an independent human or learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: A happy look is a natural noun use of look for facial expression; the second frame preserves that sense.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: حالت چهره makes the intended noun sense explicit and avoids the verb sense of look.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: Activities explicitly contrast noun look from look meaning to see.

distractorQuality.evidence: The key distractor exposes the common verb-sense confusion without ambiguity.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: A group photo provides a concrete reason to describe a facial expression.

difficultyFit.evidence: The target phrase is short; semantic distinction is the main learning load.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: The noun sense is repeated in two controlled frames.

transferQuality.evidence: Final retrieval changes from a noun phrase to a full sentence.

overallCoherence.evidence: Photo scene, noun sense and activities align.

learnerExperience.evidence: Model/editor review only; no learner test is claimed.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
Only the facial-expression noun sense is assessed.
Audio prosody is not reviewed before text gates pass.
resolvedFindings: look is intentionally authored as a noun, matching the committed reference sense.
Persian copy disambiguates the noun sense.
Walking-group arc return is spaced and learner role is rotated.
No verb sense mastery is claimed.
